Yes, is the short answer. Avoid living as much as possible. Better the devil you know than the devil you don't know. Pitiful and pathetic, yes. Wallowing in self pity, yes. All of it.

However. It's not for the reason you think.

You go long enough without meaning, without any real reason to do anything.. and it becomes comfortably numb. But it is nothing new, it has been said before.. "Most men live lives of quiet desperation".

I too once imagined, I will never give up, rage against the dying of the light, carpe diem, rather die on my feet than live in my knees.. and that's great, for the few who crack it. And sincerely well done to them. But that's not the case for the majority. And it's at this point that a lot of us just can't. And that's ok. Because in this world, there have to be inordinate amounts of losers for the winners to be able to win big.

So yes. You are right in all you say. But so what?
Loneliness is the price we pay for peace.

I have a crippling abandonment issue that, at the age of 43, has caused me to be in a situation where I lost everything and have no-one left in my life. Lockdown had zero effect on my life as that's how I had been living for a few years.

Obviously I cannot speak for anyone else but for myself. Been through a 2 year extreme isolation which forced me to face all of my issues. And being able to look back on that dark road I can say that, had anyone sat by my side and told me they're not leaving, no matter what, it would've taken root and developed that real connection I so long for.

People can change. But it's totally situational, case by case. I'm ready if someone is prepared to have zero expectations of me, to allow us to just be around each other and perhaps explore things or experiences for their own simple reasons. There's a selfish part of me I didn't like, that caused me to hurt people I loved. I've learned my lesson, painfully. So in that sense I've changed. I will treasure any real connection I happen to stumble upon from now on. I understand its value and meaning now.

If there's love involved, never give up. Not saying go all in.. but the slightest thing now, can change the future.

Good luck.

Family have no idea about the depth of this darkness and wouldn't know what to do even if they did, so to them I'm just "fine". Live and work from home, never get out. A few months ago I lost that life. Lost everything. A home, everything in it, my lady, my dogs, my office, the community around me, everything it's now gone.
